title: Security Data Bridge — Export Requirements and Connector Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This document captures a pragmatic, checklist-driven spec for exporting Redwood security and audit telemetry to customer SIEMs (Splunk, Datadog, Microsoft Sentinel) and to partner observability platforms. It focuses on customer requirements, connector-level design, RBAC v2 implications, audit log schema, evidence automation hooks, and operational constraints (throttling, redaction, retention).

Context and constraints (summary):
- Target consumers: customer security/IR teams and our SOC/Trust teams validating ingestion.
- Support model: hosted-managed connectors (Redwood-managed forwarders) and customer-managed forwarding (customer-owned HEC/collector endpoints).
- Security posture: Data must be transferable without exposing secrets; default behavior is to strip or redact PII unless explicit customer opt-in exists.
- SLAs: Best-effort delivery for non-enterprise; guaranteed ingest for Dedicated/Private customers under contractual SLAs.

1) Customer intake matrix (minimal required fields)
For each customer onboarding to export, collect the following:
- Customer SIEM type (Splunk, Datadog, Sentinel, other)
- Destination endpoint (URL), preferred protocol (HEC/HTTP/Syslog/CEF), TLS requirements
- Authentication method: token/HEC key, mTLS, Azure Event Hubs/Managed Identity, API key rotation window
- Allowed event categories: auth, admin-audit, model-inference, billing, alerting, compliance-evidence
- Redaction profile (none, default, strict) and PII policy document link
- Retention & sampling policy (retain full audit for N days / sample inference logs at X%)
- Contact(s) and escalation list (emails + paging)
- Required proofs of ingestion and evidence automation hooks (see section 6)

2) High-level connector modes
- Push-mode (Redwood-managed): Redwood sends batched events to customer endpoint. Use for customers that provide stable endpoints and trust Redwood-managed outbound traffic.
- Pull-mode (customer-managed collectors): Customer pulls from a signed S3/GCS location (short-lived URL) or subscribes to Event Hubs. Use when outbound to customer is not allowed.
- Hybrid (stream + archive): Near-real-time forwarding for alerts + batched archival export for full evidence bundles.

3) Connector spec (v0.3) - fields and behavior (this is a single-file spec used by engineering and ops)
- Protocols supported: HTTP/JSON POST, Splunk HEC, Datadog Events API, Azure Log Ingestion (Data Collector API / Event Hubs), Syslog (RFC5424) for legacy stacks.
- Batch size: default 512 events or 1 MB per batch, whichever first.
- Retry/backoff: Exponential backoff with jitter. Retries up to 5 attempts over 30 minutes before marking events as failed and writing to quarantine.
- Failure handling: store failed batches in encrypted, short-lived blob store (7 days) for re-delivery or customer pull.
- Authentication: token header (Authorization: Bearer <token>) or HEC token header (Authorization: Splunk <token>) or mTLS. Support token rotation by accepting previous token for grace period of 24 hours.
- Idempotency: include "redwood_event_id" and "ingest_sequence" in each event; dest should tolerate duplicates.
- Throttling: honor 429 with Retry-After; if missing, backoff using policy. Track observed RPS and drop lower-priority events (inference traces) when saturated.

4) Event shape and minimal audit schema (recommended canonical fields)
We push a canonical JSON envelope to simplify downstream correlation. Minimal required fields:
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC string
- event_type: one of [auth, admin, api_call, inference, model_load, deployment, alert, billing, evidence]
- redwood_event_id: UUIDv4 string (unique per event)
- request_id: customer-visible request id (if available)
- actor: short struct flattened as actor_type and actor_id (e.g., actor_type=user, actor_id=alice@example.com OR actor_type=svc, actor_id=svc-infer-42)
- resource: resource_type and resource_id (e.g., model, deployment, route)
- outcome: success | failure | partial
- outcome_reason: short message (optional)
- details: free-form message or compact JSON string with non-sensitive fields
- severity: numeric or string mapped to SIEM locale (default mapping: info=3, notice=4, warning=5, error=7, critical=9)
- tenant_id: customer id (for multi-tenant customers using single endpoint)
- rb_role_change: optional: when RBAC v2 role changes occur include role_name, change_type (grant/revoke), actor_id
- audit_version: "v1"

Sample event (as JSON string inside content):
{
  "timestamp": "2025-02-01T15:12:32Z",
  "event_type": "admin",
  "redwood_event_id": "b3f2c1d0-9c6a-4f2a-8d2e-1234567890ab",
  "request_id": "req_0b12f...",
  "actor_type": "user",
  "actor_id": "security@acme-corp.com",
  "resource_type": "rbac_role",
  "resource_id": "role-readonly-123",
  "outcome": "success",
  "details": "Granted role to user via UI",
  "severity": "notice",
  "tenant_id": "acct-9876",
  "audit_version": "v1"
}

5) Field mapping guidance for common SIEMs
- Splunk HEC: send the entire JSON envelope into the HEC _raw field and set index, source, sourcetype headers. Add Splunk metadata: event_time=timestamp, host=redwood.redwood-inference.com, sourcetype=redwood:audit:v1. Recommend compressed gzip POST when payload >1MB.
- Datadog: use Logs API with attributes tagging. Map tenant_id to dd.source and add dd.service=redwood-inference. Include redwood_event_id as dd.trace_id to tie logs to traces in Datadog APM if applicable.
- Sentinel (Log Analytics / Data Collector API): map top-level keys to custom fields; include "TenantId_s" and "EventType_s" suffix conventions for Kusto. Support batching into JSON array payloads up to Azure limits (30 MB).

6) Evidence automation and audit trace attachments
- Evidence bundles: Some compliance customers require the ability to request evidence for a specific audit window or request_id. The connector should support producing an evidence bundle containing: the primary events, associated inference inputs (if allowed by contract), model version fingerprints, and signed integrity manifest (SHA256).
- Automation API: provide a signed, short-lived download link to a zipped evidence bundle when requested via Support API. Logged actions (who requested evidence) must themselves be emitted as audit events.
- Data minimization: by default redact raw model inputs from exported bundles unless customer checks the explicit opt-in checkbox during onboarding and signs the required data processing addendum.

7) RBAC v2 considerations
- Role-change events must include before/after snapshots when possible. For changes via API or UI, include granularity: permissions_added:[], permissions_removed:[], scope_changes:[] fields.
- Export access control: require a dedicated export role (export-siem) that is mapped to service principal used by the connector. This role must be documented in RBAC policies and limited to read-only access to audit logs and delivery configuration.

8) Privacy, redaction, and allowed PII patterns
- Default-redaction list: email addresses, full user ids, input text longer than 256 chars, client IPs (unless requested), tokens. Replace with pseudonyms: user_email -> user_pseudonym (hash: sha256(lowercase(email)) truncated to 12 chars).
- Redaction strategy: deterministic hashing for correlation plus field-level suppression for sensitive content. Provide an option for tokenization (token vault) for customers with strict retention needs.

9) Operational runbook (SRE + SOC playbook snippets)
- On 429/slow responses: scale to smaller batch sizes and increase flush frequency for realtime events.
- On auth failures: rotate and re-deploy token; alert customer contact; point to mitigation page.
- On data mismatch complaints: support retrieving raw batch from quarantine and provide signed integrity manifest.
- Monitor metrics: outbound success rate, avg latency, 99th percentile per-destination latency, drop-rate, and quarantine size. Emit these metrics into Redwood observability with dashboards per-customer.

10) Testing checklist before go-live
- Connectivity test (TLS handshake and cert validation)
- Auth test (token acceptance and rotation grace period)
- Throughput/latency test at expected peak load + 30% headroom
- Redaction verification (sample set of events containing PII)
- Evidence bundle generation + signed manifest validation
- Duplicate suppression/idempotency test
- End-to-end ingestion sample event validated by customer SIEM team (provide test token and sample event)

11) Example configurations and snippets
- Splunk HEC POST sample headers:
  Authorization: Splunk <HEC_TOKEN>
  X-Splunk-Request-Id: <redwood_event_id>
  Content-Type: application/json

- Datadog example: send event with tags: ["tenant:acct-9876", "env:prod", "source:redwood"] and include request_id as attribute.

12) Open questions and action items
- Should we standardize on a single canonical envelope field naming for all destinations to reduce transform logic in connectors? (ops + eng to decide)
- Confirm which customers will require raw-model-input export (legal + product).
- Run a security review of token rotation and whether we should support customer-provided KMS-wrapped tokens for HEC keys.

Appendix: quick-reference mapping
- redwood_event_id -> unique id for deduplication
- tenant_id -> customer account id
- actor_type/actor_id -> who performed the action
- resource_type/resource_id -> object acted on
- details -> non-sensitive contextual info
- audit_version -> schema version for parsing

Contact and escalation: Priya Menon (security), Ethan Zhao (platform eng), Laura Kim (customer success).

Notes: This file is intended to be used as the canonical onboarding checklist for SIEM exports and as the connector design brief for the engineering implementation of the managed forwarder. It intentionally prioritizes operational simplicity, deterministic redaction for downstream investigation, and contractual controls for sensitive input export.
